entry.title: Trivia Game v9.0.0: Settings window in UIFramework, an OBS overlay & your questions mixed into any source
entry.content:
The settings window moves into UIFramework for streamer.bot, the window all of these chat games now share, and reads in English or German. Rounds can now show up in OBS, your own questions mix with any source, and your own actions can react to every round. configs.json and Trivia-Questions.json keep working: old keys are read and written back under their new names on the first save.

📺 An OBS overlay for the running round

  • A browser source that shows the question with its numbered options, a countdown and how many have answered, then the right answer, the winners with their points and the top of the leaderboard. Blitz rounds are marked in red. It listens to Streamer.bot's own WebSocket server, so there is nothing else to install.
  • Set it up in OBS adds the source the size of your canvas to a scene of your choice, through Streamer.bot's OBS connection. Show a sample round plays one on every connected overlay, Try the demo in the browser.
  • Its look from the Overlay page: position, size, animations, five colours and the panel's opacity. A save reaches an overlay already open in OBS.

🪟 One settings window for all the chat games

  • Downloaded on first open. [TG] - Settings is now a small stub. The first time you open it, it offers to download UIFramework.dll from GitHub (checked against its published SHA-256) or to show the folder it belongs in. Newer releases are offered when you open the window, never forced; "autoUpdate": false in uiframework.layout.json turns the check off.
  • English or German. The pencil, then Sprache: every setting, section, page, option and message reads in German.
  • Customise mode. Rename, reorder, hide and move pages and fields by drag and drop, pick the accent colour. It lives in uiframework.layout.json and survives every import of the game.
  • The question list is a table edited in place: one line per question, a click into a cell edits it, a checkbox in every row switches it on or off, Delete removes the picked rows, a search box above. Suggested by is filled by the game and only read here.
  • The difficulty dial is a slider with the same stops, Relaxed to Brutal, filling in the same six numbers.

🌍 Questions from anywhere, yours mixed in

  • Mix in my questions on the Sources page mixes your own list into whichever source is picked: opentdb, Wikidata, OdeNet, PokeAPI or IGDB. Share of mine says how often. Mine + opentdb is gone from the dropdown; a configs.json with it is rewritten as opentdb with mixing on.
  • A tidier Sources page. Source, language and Check share one line, only the picked source is described, the IGDB keys only show while IGDB is picked, and the Client Secret and the overlay's WebSocket password are masked.

🔔 For your own actions

  • Custom triggers carry the round. Trivia: Round Won, Round Timeout, Round Skipped and Round ForceEnd fire with roundOutcome, roundPlatform, roundId, roundBlitz, roundQuestion, roundCorrectAnswer, roundCategory, roundDifficulty, roundSource, roundAnswers, roundWinners, roundWinnerCount, roundPoints and roundCurrency.
  • GetLastRoundResult, run with an Execute C# Method sub-action on the game action, hands the same arguments to any other action.

⚙️ Settings file

  • Keys are camelCase now; CooldownGlobalSeconds, CooldownUserSeconds, VarName, UseBotCD and SendActionCD are globalCooldown, userCooldown, pointsVariable, cooldownUseBot and cooldownSendAction. An existing file keeps working through aliases; the first save writes the new names.
  • The wrong answers are written to Trivia-Questions.json as a | b | c text; the game reads that and the old array alike.
  • Light/dark lives in uiframework.layout.json, shared with every other window built on UIFramework.

🔧 Fixed

  • A number box left empty, or holding half a number, stops the save instead of going in as 0.
  • The theme button asks before it switches when there are unsaved changes.
  • No label shows its unit twice any more ("(%) (%)", "(s) (s)").

🗑️ Removed

  • The window's own WPF code (about 6,800 lines) left the import; the DLL carries it now. The rail's keyboard shortcuts went with it.

Updating

Import TriviaGame.sb below, or the import string, over the existing actions. Your settings, your questions and the scoreboard stay where they are. The overlay stays off until you switch it on.

Download v9.0.0 · Trivia Game on aaskjer.github.io

entry.title: High-Low Game v2.1.0: Higher, lower or the same, guess to find out
entry.content:
The first release of High-Low Game on GitHub. There is always a number from 1 to 100 waiting; viewers guess whether the next one is higher, lower or the same, on Twitch, YouTube and Kick. The settings window is UIFramework for streamer.bot, the window all of these chat games share, in English or German.

🎲 The game

  • A number from the start. The game draws one for each platform when Streamer.bot starts, so nobody has to run !highlowsetup first. Moderators can still draw and announce a fresh one with it.
  • !high, !low and !equal. A correct high or low pays the win amount, a wrong one costs nothing; !equal pays double and costs the win amount when wrong. The answer names both numbers.
  • Scoreboards. !hlgsession, !hlgalltime and !hlgpersonal, with the broadcaster and the bot account left out if you want.

🎫 Channel points on Twitch

  • Three rewards, one each for high, low and equal. Paste their IDs on the Channel points page; the import already carries the reward trigger.
  • Stakes: Cost and Fixed spend the channel points and pay a correct guess in points, Input takes a bet in the viewer's own points (all, half, 2k, …), Free plays like the chat commands. Minimum and maximum bet apply.
  • Refunds. A redemption that does not end in a guess is refunded, a played one is marked as fulfilled.

🪟 One settings window for all the chat games

  • Downloaded on first open. [HLG] - .Settings is UIFramework's small settings stub. The first time you open it, it offers to download UIFramework.dll from GitHub (checked against its published SHA-256) or to show the folder it belongs in. Nothing is fetched without that click; newer releases are offered when you open the window, never forced.
  • English or German. The pencil, then Sprache: every setting, section, page and message reads in German.
  • Customise mode. Rename, reorder, hide and move pages and fields, pick the accent colour. It lives in uiframework.layout.json next to HLG-Settings.json and survives every import.
  • Cooldowns per command, written onto the Streamer.bot commands when you save, and every chat line editable with a live preview.

🔔 For your own actions

  • Custom triggers (Custom > Chat Game > High-Low Game): HLG: Guess Won, HLG: Guess Lost and HLG: Guess Settled for every guess, HLG: New Number when !highlowsetup draws one.
  • The guess as arguments: guessOutcome, guessUser, guessPlatform, guessGuess, guessPreviousNumber, guessNewNumber, guessMode, guessStake, guessAmount, guessPreviousPoints, guessNewPoints, guessCurrency, guessFree and more. GetLastGuessResult, run with an Execute C# Method sub-action on the game action, hands them to any other action.

🆓 Free mode

  • A switch on the Game page, or !SetFreeHighLow / !EndFreeHighLow from chat (moderators). Nobody wins or loses points, the guesses still count. The two commands come with the import, disabled: enable them in Streamer.bot's Commands tab if you want them.
  • HLG: Free Game Start and HLG: Free Game End fire when it is switched, from chat or by an Execute C# Method on StartFreeGame or EndFreeGame, and chat gets a Started and an Ended line.

💰 Points

  • Works with Currency Core by StreamUP and LOYALTY POINTS by tawmae: whichever is installed names the points variable and the points name. Anything else works too; name its variable on the Game page.

Installing

Import HighLowGame.sb below, or the import string, then open the settings with the Test trigger of [HLG] - .Settings. The setup guide walks through every page.

Coming from an earlier copy of the game? Import over the existing actions: HLG-Settings.json stays where it is, old setting names are read until the window saves them under the new ones, and old cooldown messages with {0} and {1} still work. Trovo support and the per-platform switches are gone; leave a platform out by unticking its source on the commands.

Download v2.1.0 · High-Low Game on aaskjer.github.io

entry.title: RhymeTime v2.2.0: One settings window, hooks for your own actions, Free mode from chat
entry.content:
The settings window moves into UIFramework for streamer.bot, the window all of these chat games now share, and reads in English or German. The game and the battle play as before, your own actions can now react to every round and battle, and moderators can switch Free mode from chat. RT-settings.json and RT-wordbank.json keep working: old keys are read and written back under their new names on the first save.

🪟 One settings window for all the chat games

  • Downloaded on first open. [RT] - Settings is now a small stub. The first time you open it, it offers to download UIFramework.dll from GitHub (checked against its published SHA-256) or to show the folder it belongs in. Nothing is fetched without that click. Newer releases are offered when you open the window, never forced; "autoUpdate": false in uiframework.layout.json turns the check off.
  • English or German. The pencil, then Sprache: every setting, section, page and message reads in German.
  • The word banks are a table. All three sit on the Word banks page, one word per line, edited where it stands, with a search box above, Add row, Remove row (or Delete) and Restore defaults. Still saved into RT-wordbank.json, the file the game and the battle read.
  • Customise mode. Rename, reorder, hide and move pages and fields by drag and drop, pick the accent colour. It lives in uiframework.layout.json next to RT-settings.json and survives every import of the game.
  • The game answers the window. The Overlay page's buttons and the check before saving run in the game, and the window is built from the game's own settings table, so the two can never disagree about a key, a default or a range.

📺 The overlay

  • Show a sample round. A button beside Set the overlay up in OBS plays one made-up round on every open overlay, the one in OBS included, in the look saved on the Overlay page. It waits while a real round or battle is on.
  • An Overlay pill in the header says whether rounds reach the OBS overlay, like the Free game pill.

🔔 For your own actions

  • Custom triggers (Custom > Chat Game > RhymeTime): RT: Round Won, RT: Round Lost, RT: Round Timeout and RT: Round Settled every time; RT: Battle Won, RT: Battle Timeout and RT: Battle Settled for a battle; RT: Free Game Start and RT: Free Game End.
  • The round as arguments: roundOutcome, roundUser, roundPlatform, roundWord, roundGuess, roundDifficulty, roundBet, roundAmount, roundAttempts, roundPreviousPoints, roundNewPoints, roundCurrency, roundFree, and for a battle battleOutcome, battleWinner, battleWord, battleStake, battleReward, battleStarter and more. GetLastRoundResult and GetLastBattleResult, run with an Execute C# Method sub-action, hand the same arguments to any other action.

🆓 Free mode, and from chat

  • A Free mode switch on the Game page (a default bet of 0 is free as before).
  • !SetFreeRhyme and !EndFreeRhyme (moderators) switch it from chat. They come with the import, disabled: enable them in Streamer.bot's Commands tab if you want them. The switch is written into the settings file, so the window's pill shows it, and chat gets the new Started and Ended lines (Messages page, Free mode).

⚙️ Settings file

  • Keys are camelCase now (useBot, minBet, globalCooldown, overlayAccentColour). An existing file keeps working through aliases; the first save writes the new names.
  • Light/dark and the rainbow mode live in uiframework.layout.json, shared with every other window built on UIFramework. An existing DarkMode is taken over on the first open.
  • Values typed out of range are pulled back into range when the game reads them, not only when the window saves.

🔧 Fixed

  • A damaged RT-wordbank.json is no longer quietly thrown away. The game sets it aside as RT-wordbank.json.broken, falls back to the .bak from before the last save, and never writes the shipped words over a file somebody typed into.

🗑️ Removed

  • The window's own WPF code and update check (about 4,500 lines) left the import; the DLL carries them now.

Updating

Import RhymeTime.sb below, or the import string, over the existing actions. Your settings, word banks and player statistics stay where they are. The two Free mode commands arrive disabled. The Setup Guide walks through the first open.

entry.title: Hangman Game v13.0.0: The settings window moves into UIFramework
entry.content:
The settings window moves into UIFramework for streamer.bot, the window all of these chat games now share, and reads in English or German. The game plays as before; on top come a Free mode you can switch from chat, the round as arguments for your own actions, and a demo for the overlay. configs.json keeps working: old keys are read and written back under their new names on the first save.

🪟 One settings window for all the chat games

  • Downloaded on first open. [HM] - Settings is now a small stub. The first time you open it, it offers to download UIFramework.dll from GitHub (checked against its published SHA-256) or to show the folder it belongs in. Nothing is fetched without that click. Newer releases are offered when you open the window, never forced; "autoUpdate": false in uiframework.layout.json turns the check off.
  • The same pages: Game, Words, Overlay, Access, Messages, Board and Log, plus a help page and an about page.
  • English or German. The pencil, then Sprache: every setting, section, page and message reads in German, the word list's column headers included.
  • Customise mode. Rename, reorder, hide and move pages and fields by drag and drop, pick the accent colour. It lives in uiframework.layout.json next to configs.json and survives every import of the game.
  • The game answers the window. The OBS buttons, Create the browser source in OBS and Refresh the overlay in OBS, answer in the window's footer instead of a message box; Open the word list folder and Open the overlay folder sit next to what they open.

📚 Words

  • The word list is a table, edited in place: a click into a cell edits it, a search box above, several rows picked and removed at once (Remove row or Delete).
  • Importing words is a section of the Words page: source (Wikidata, OdeNet, PokéAPI, IGDB), topic, language, limits and difficulty as fields, then Import now. The fetched words skip what the list already holds and show in the list right away. The IGDB client ID and secret are kept in Streamer.bot's global variables after the first import, never in configs.json.
  • Categories in play became Categories left out: type a category name and press Enter to leave it out.

🆓 Free mode

  • A switch on the Game page and a pill in the header: letters and wins pay nothing while it is on.
  • !SetFreeHangman and !EndFreeHangman (moderators) switch it from chat. They come with the import, disabled: enable them in Streamer.bot's Commands tab if you want them. Chat gets a Started and an Ended line.

🔔 For your own actions

  • The round as arguments. Hangman: Game Win, Game Loss, Game Stopped and Timeout now carry the round: roundOutcome, roundWord, roundCategory, roundDifficulty, roundLetters, roundPlatform, roundWinner, roundWinnerId, roundPoints, roundWrongGuesses, roundMaxWrong, roundBlitz, roundFree, roundCurrency, roundParticipants; the same in the globals hm_last…, and GetLastRoundResult, run with an Execute C# Method sub-action on the game action, hands them to any other action.
  • Hangman: Free Game Start and Hangman: Free Game End fire when Free mode is switched, from chat or by an Execute C# Method on StartFreeGame or EndFreeGame.

📺 Overlay

  • Try the demo opens the overlay in your browser, playing made-up rounds without Streamer.bot in the colours and sizes you saved; &demo=1 at the end of the OBS source's address does the same, to place and size it.
  • Show a sample round plays one made-up round on the live overlay, the one in OBS included: letters, wrong guesses, an Evil Hangman swap and a win, then puts the overlay back as it was. It refuses while a real round runs.
  • The overlay is version 10 and replaces an older copy on the next round, keeping that one as a .bak.

⚙️ Settings file and log

  • Keys are new (maxWrongGuesses, msgGameStart, …); an existing configs.json keeps working through aliases, and the first save writes the new names. OverlayBackgroundOpacity is stored as a percent now (an old 0.5 reads as 50). messages.json from before v12 is still read for a message the settings file does not hold.
  • Light/dark lives in uiframework.layout.json, shared with every other window built on UIFramework; an existing DarkMode is taken over on the first open.
  • Values typed out of range (no lives, chances outside 0 to 100, the overlay scale below 10 %, …) are pulled back into range when the game reads them, not only when the window saves.
  • The log in the framework's format. Lines read [time] RESULT | User: … | Platform: … | Round: … | …, which the Log page filters by result, platform and day; files from before v13 show as raw lines. Write a log file per day sits on the Log page.

🗑️ Removed

  • The window's own WPF code (about 6,000 lines) left the import; the DLL carries it now.
  • The Egg mode; the customise mode has a rainbow of its own.
  • The import preview with ticks before anything is added.

Updating

Import HangmanGame.sb below, or the import string, over the existing actions. Your settings, word list and scoreboard stay where they are. The two Free mode commands arrive disabled.

Download v13.0.0 · Hangman Game on aaskjer.github.io

entry.title: Slot Machine Game v16.2.0: Emotes like chat, Free mode from chat, hooks for your own actions
entry.content:
Emote lists that read like chat, YouTube's own emojis, Free mode from chat, and hooks for your own actions. Import SlotMachineGame.sb over the old one — SMG-Settings.json is yours and stays where it is. The spin plays as before.

😀 Emotes

  • No name column. The name of an emote is in its code: a Twitch emote is its name (case-sensitive), a Kick emote's name follows its ID, a YouTube emoji's name sits between its colons. The weight column is last and half as wide, so long emote names stay readable.
  • YouTube's own emojis. The YouTube list takes the emojis YouTube's chat has, typed as :name: like :face-purple-rain-drops:, shows their pictures and starts with ten of them. The fruit emoji of earlier versions were only emotes to viewers with BetterTTV. A Unicode emoji still works and shows itself.
  • Kick typed short. 1730803:emojiRich is enough; the game sends it as [emote:1730803:emojiRich], the form Kick's chat renders. The full form still works in the list.

🆓 Free mode from chat

  • !SetFreeSlots and !EndFreeSlots (moderators) switch Free mode from chat. They come with the import, disabled: enable them in Streamer.bot's Commands tab if you want them. The switch is written into the settings file, so the window's pill shows it, and chat gets the new Started and Ended lines (Messages page, Free mode).

🔔 For your own actions

  • Custom triggers (Custom > Chat Game > Slot Machine Game): SMG: Spin Win, SMG: Spin Loss, SMG: Spin Jackpot, SMG: Spin Free on top of those for a free spin, and SMG: Free Game Start / SMG: Free Game End when Free mode is switched.
  • The spin as arguments: spinOutcome, spinUser, spinPlatform, spinSlots, spinBet, spinAmount, spinPreviousPoints, spinNewPoints, spinCurrency, spinJackpotPoolWon, spinFree. GetLastSpinResult, run with an Execute C# Method sub-action on the game action, hands them to any other action; StartFreeGame and EndFreeGame switch Free mode the same way.
  • Stats per viewer in Streamer.bot's user variables, for a leaderboard of your own: smg_spins, smg_wins, smg_losses, smg_jackpots, smg_totalBet, smg_totalWon, smg_totalLost, smg_netProfit, smg_biggestWin, smg_biggestBet, smg_poolWon, smg_currentStreak, smg_bestStreak, smg_userName, smg_firstPlayed, smg_lastPlayed.

🪟 Settings window

  • German. The pencil, then Sprache: every setting, section, page and message reads in German.
  • The settings action is UIFramework's generic stub. [SMG] - Settings carries no layout of its own any more; the game declares its window and answers it, the test spin included. The stub keeps UIFramework current.
  • The comment lines in Streamer.bot's sub-action list follow the other games: title, a pointer to the settings, the chat commands.

Prefer pasting over downloading? The import string is the same thing. The Setup Guide walks through the window, and questions are answered in the FAQ.

entry.title: Battleship Game v2.0.0: The settings window moves into UIFramework
entry.content:
The settings window moved into UIFramework for streamer.bot, one window shared by all of these chat games. Import BattleshipGame.sb over the old one — BSG-Settings.json is yours and stays where it is — then open [BG] - .Settings and answer Yes once. Battles, the chat's battle and the duel play exactly as before; what changed is how the settings are shown and stored.

🪟 One window, downloaded on first open

  • [BG] - .Settings is a small stub now. The first time you open it, it asks whether to download UIFramework.dll from GitHub (about 200 KB, checked against its published SHA-256) or to show the folder it belongs in, UIFramework\lib\<version>\ next to Streamer.bot. Nothing is fetched without that click. When a newer UIFramework is published, opening the window offers it once: Yes downloads, No asks again next time and shows a pill in the header, Cancel skips that version.
  • The window is built from the game's own settings table. The game declares every setting once, the scoreboard carries the same table, and the window asks the game for it, so the window and the actions can never disagree about a key, a default or a range again.
  • The Fleet page keeps its presets and its summary. Blitz, Quick and Classic fill in the board and the ships as before, and the line under the ships says how many squares the fleet takes and about how many shots a battle needs, as the values stand. The battle clock has the same kind of summary on the Game page.
  • The Clicks page shows the broadcaster account Streamer.bot is connected to, and still adds Heat's click markers to OBS with one button.
  • A save that would not do what it looks like asks first: Free game off without a points variable, no ship sailing, a ship longer than the board, a warning that is not shorter than a turn, Click to Fire without a WebSocket address.
  • Customise mode. The pencil at the bottom left lets you rename, reorder, hide and move pages and fields by drag and drop or from the context menu, and pick the accent colour. It lives in uiframework.layout.json next to BSG-Settings.json and survives every import of the game.
  • The footer counts the unsaved changes; a third button resets only the page in front, after asking; Cancel and the title bar's X ask "Discard N unsaved changes?" before dropping anything; a recompile or shutdown of Streamer.bot closes an open window on its way out.

⚙️ Settings

  • BSG-Settings.json keys are camelCase now (freeGame, gridSize, overlayHitColour, heatEnabled), the percentages (the Addicted cut, the overlay scales and opacity, the blunder chance, the Heat area) are stored as percent instead of fractions, and "Battles per hour" stores 0 for no limit. An existing file keeps working: the old names are read through aliases and scaled on the way, and the first save writes the new ones.
  • The cooldown messages use {seconds} and {user} instead of {0} and {1}; a text that still has the numbers keeps working.
  • Light/dark lives in uiframework.layout.json and is shared with every other window built on UIFramework. An existing DarkMode is taken over on the first open.
  • Values typed out of range are pulled back into range when the game reads them, not only when the window saves.
  • The fleet whisper switch sits on the Access page under Platforms.

🗑️ Removed

  • The window's own WPF code and update check (about 4,500 lines) left the import; the DLL carries them now.

Prefer pasting over downloading? The import string is the same thing. The Setup Guide walks through the first open and the customise mode, and questions are answered in the FAQ.

Changed

In v2.1.0 the GameVox and Stoat messages were copies that followed the Discord post, so they were only posted together with a new Discord announcement and a failed Discord post or edit held them back. entry.title: RhymeTime v1.0.0: The first release
entry.content:
The first release. Import RhymeTime.sb, enable the two commands, and open [RT] - Settings with a right-click on its Test trigger — the Setup Guide walks through it.

🎮The game

  • !Rhyme draws a word and gives the chatter a clock and a handful of attempts to rhyme with it. Answers go into ordinary chat — only the last word of the message is read, so "hmm maybe DREAM" counts.
  • Rhymes nobody listed still count. The rhymes you write are examples: the longest ending enough of them share becomes what the round accepts, so BAT, HAT, MAT takes any dictionary word ending in AT. A listed rhyme always counts, the target word never does, and a guess that does not even end the right way is ignored instead of costing an attempt.
  • Lines to finish. A target with spaces in it is a line to complete rather than a word to rhyme, and the whole reply has to match one of the answers you listed.
  • !RhymeBattle opens one word to the whole chat. The first valid rhyme takes the prize; nobody else pays anything. Moderators only, one battle per platform.

💰Points

  • A win pays the stake times the multiplier of the bank the word came from, a loss costs the stake, and a battle pays the moderator's stake or a flat reward. A battle nobody wins hands the stake back.
  • Chatters bet a number, or all, half, third, quarter, random, framed by a minimum and a maximum. Put the default bet at 0 and the whole game is free — nothing staked, nothing paid.
  • Currency Core by StreamUP and LOYALTY POINTS by tawmae are found on their own; the Game page is only for a points system of your own.

⚙️The settings window

  • Seven pages — Game, Battle, Word banks, Access, Messages, How to play, About — with Ctrl+1…Ctrl+7, Ctrl+S, light and dark, a count of what you changed and warnings about settings that cancel each other out.
  • A word-bank editor for the three banks, with Restore this bank for the words RhymeTime ships.
  • All 19 chat lines in one place, grouped by when they are sent, with clickable placeholders and a live preview of how each will read in chat.
  • Settings and word banks are written atomically: the previous copy is kept as .bak, and a damaged file is set aside as .broken instead of being overwritten.

🌐Everywhere

Twitch, YouTube and Kick all play, always, with the reply going back to the chat the command came from. There is no platform selection — restrict the commands in Streamer.bot instead.

entry.title: Better Stream Announcements v2.1.0: Stoat & GameVox copies, a new Settings window and a color picker
entry.content:
Announcements can now go to GameVox and Stoat as well, the Settings window is rebuilt around a sidebar with a Home page and a Status Log, and every embed color gets a color picker. Nothing to redo after the update: the new webhook fields start empty, and while they are empty everything is posted exactly as before.

Added

  • A copy of every announcement on GameVox and Stoat. Broadcaster → Platforms and Streamer Friends → Platforms each take an optional GameVox webhook and an optional Stoat webhook. The copy follows the Discord message: updated with it and switched to its ended form when the stream ends. Your own announcement's copy also comes back with it within the revive window, and a Streamer Friend's copy is deleted together with the Discord message once Remove Old Message takes it down. It is only posted together with a new announcement, so a webhook added while someone is live starts with their next stream. Every call is best effort: one retry after a rate limit or a server error, a failure is logged, and Discord carries on either way.
    • GameVox gets the Discord post without buttons, role mentions and the embed timestamp, whose time moves into the footer (“LIVE since • 2026-10-25 20:15”).
    • Stoat (formerly Revolt) has no author line, fields or footer in its embeds, so the author line goes in bold above the embed and the fields and footer become lines of the description. No preview picture: Stoat only takes pictures uploaded through a bot account.
  • Home page: who is live right now and where announcements go, a five-step Start Here (can be hidden), today's warnings and errors at a glance, and help links.
  • Status Log page (Help → Status Log): everything BsA wrote to Streamer.bot's log, one day at a time, including the errors Streamer.bot reports about a BsA action. Filter by day, action, level and text.
  • Color picker on every embed color. A swatch beside each hex box shows the color; a click opens a picker right under the field — a saturation and brightness field with a hue bar to click or drag, sliders for red, green and blue (the mouse wheel nudges them by one), and the colors Discord uses most. Every change goes straight into the hex box, and typing a hex code moves the picker along.

Changed

  • The Settings window is rebuilt around a sidebar. The nested tabs are gone: the pages sit in four groups — Broadcaster, Streamer Friends, Discord Bot, Help — under the names they had as tabs. Ctrl+F searches every setting, the footer counts unsaved changes, Save (Ctrl+S) keeps the window open and Save & Exit closes it, and closing with unsaved changes asks first. Theme and reset sit in the ☰ menu.

Fixed

  • Placeholders for Owncast, Picarto, Rumble and TikTok friends. {user}, {title}, {game}, {url} and {viewers} came out as literal text, since these four only took %user% and the like. Both forms work now.
  • {game} on YouTube is empty instead of literal text, since YouTube gives no category.

Removed

entry.title: Chat Calendar v1.0.0: Chat Calendar v1.0.0
entry.content:
Twitch Calendar is now Chat Calendar: holiday and birthday greetings on Twitch, YouTube and Kick, a daily post to Discord, Stoat and GameVox, and one settings window for all of it. Nothing has to be run by hand any more — the window downloads the holidays itself.

✨Added

  • A settings window. Right-click the Test trigger of [CC] - .Settings and choose Test Trigger. Chat, Announcements, Calendar, Holidays, Birthdays, Messages and Log, with Help and About at the foot: every greeting with a chat preview, your own holidays and the greeting of every official one, the birthdays, the webhooks and the log of what was said and posted. It saves configs.json next to holidays.json; a damaged file is kept as configs.json.broken and the window falls back to the last save. A red pill in its header shows when a newer release is out.
  • YouTube and Kick. Chatters there are greeted on holidays and on their birthday, and every command answers in the chat it came from.
  • Birthdays. Viewers save their own with !birthday 24.12. (day and month only); moderators and you for others with !birthday @name 24.12.. Everyone is greeted once on their day, with {age} where the Birthdays page knows the year. !nextbirthdays lists the next ones.
  • Announcements. Today's holidays and birthdays go to Discord, Stoat and GameVox once a day, at the time you set — no Streamer.bot timer needed. A failed webhook is tried again after 15 minutes, without posting twice to the ones that worked. Title, lines and colour are yours, the colour with a picker.
  • Own days. Channel birthday, charity stream, anything: once on a date, or every year (12-24 or 24.12.).
  • Regions. Only the holidays of your region, if you pick one — Bavaria, Vienna, Zürich … — or only the nationwide ones.
  • Bot or broadcaster, and on Twitch as a /me message.

🔧Changed

  • No more Set Argument sub-actions. Every setting lives in the window. An argument of the same name in an action still wins, for a second action that should do something else.
  • Nothing to run by hand. .. Setup Action .. is now [CC] - Calendar Setup without a trigger: the window starts it when it opens without this year's holidays, after saving another country, region, time zone or year, and from Save and download now. A new year downloads itself.
  • Every chatter is greeted once per holiday, also when the stream runs past midnight, in the time zone you set.
  • All data lives in Chat Calendar next to Streamer.bot: holidays.json, birthdays.json, configs.json and a Logs folder kept for 30 days. Your own holidays and greetings survive every download.
  • Texts follow your country, or the chat language you pick; Boarisch writes Bavarian.

🐛Fixed

  • Holidays download again. date.nager.at dropped its CSV export; Chat Calendar uses its JSON API.
  • {holidayName} was empty, and two holidays on one day were announced as one.
  • The command answered nothing on a day without a holiday.
  • !nextholidays failed for countries without a translation (AT, CH, GB, PL …).
  • No more Hello @, without a user name, and no error in the log for every viewer without pronouns.

⬆️Updating from Twitch Calendar

Import over the old version. Your holidays (C:\streamer.bot\Twitch Calendar or Twitch Calendar next to Streamer.bot) are copied into Chat Calendar on the first run, with your own holidays and greetings; the country, region and time zone come along. Webhook URLs and your own texts from the old Set Argument sub-actions are entered once in the settings window. The commands ship switched off: enable them under Commands.

Import the attached ChatCalendar.sb, or paste the import string. The Setup Guide walks through every page.

entry.title: OBS Notes v1.0.0: Initial Release
entry.content:
First release.

  • Viewers save short notes with !note, read them back with !zettel; moderators and VIPs delete one with !radier <number> or all with !clearnotes. Every game (Twitch category) keeps its own list.

  • Notes added at the same moment are all kept, and a crash while saving never leaves a broken file behind.
  • Times in chat are shown in the streamer's local time; a note too long for one chat message is shortened.

entry.title: Blackjack Game v16.2.1: Atomic saves and a settings file that can be rescued
entry.content:
A hardening release for the settings file. BJG-Settings.json is read as it stands — no setting changes, and nothing to redo after the update.

💾The settings file

  • Saving is atomic. BJG-Settings.json was written straight over itself, so a crash halfway through could leave a truncated file behind — the game reads it on every hand. It is now written beside the live one and swapped in, and every save leaves BJG-Settings.json.bak, the file as it was before that save.
  • A damaged file is reported in the window and kept as BJG-Settings.json.broken. The window shows the settings from before the last save, or the defaults when there is no readable backup. Until now a read error raised an "Error loading settings" box from Streamer.bot's own thread — a modal dialog with no window behind it, holding the action until somebody found it — and then carried on with the defaults, which the next save wrote over the damaged file without a word.
  • A file that cannot be opened at all no longer opens the window. It said "damaged" and showed the defaults, so a save would overwrite a perfectly good file that was merely locked.
  • A settings file the game script is holding open is waited out instead of failing on the first try.

⏱️Cooldowns and the window

  • The cooldowns of !blackjack, !duel and !house were set from the settings window's own thread. All six are now handed to Streamer.bot's thread while the window is open, as one set, so they can never be applied as a mix of two saves.
  • Only one settings window opens. A second trigger while it was up opened another one with its own copy of the settings, and whichever was saved last won. It now brings the open window to the front.
  • Switching pages redraws only the page in front, instead of every control in the window.
